Thanks — I pulled the forecast and ran a quick model. Key bullets (high level):

- Perf/$ snapshot (sustained inference, ranking workloads, 512 tokens):
  • H100 80GB: best raw throughput, approx 1.8–2.2x tokens/sec vs A100 80GB on our kernels, ~18–22% higher list price than A100 but 25–30% better perf/$ because of throughput.
  • A100 80GB: predictable memory, good latency for medium batch sizes; lower unit price but higher per-token cost for high-throughput workloads.
  • L40S 48GB: lowest list price; strong for smaller models and embedding-heavy workloads, but memory limits can force model splits or more frequent KV reloads for large-recall ranking models.

- Memory considerations: if your models keep 40–60GB KV caches per replica, A100 80GB and H100 80GB are safe. L40S triggers cache fragmentation and increases tail latency unless we shard KV across nodes.

- Recommended commit structures (based on forecast peaks and 99th pct headroom):
  Option A — H100-heavy: 8x H100-80GB reserved (24-month) + 2x burst H100 on demand. Recommended for latency-sensitive ranking; we can guarantee 95th-pct token throughput at X tokens/sec per GPU (see attached term sheet). Estimated discount: 24-month commit -> 28% off list; 12-month -> 18% off.
  Option B — Mixed pool (cost optimized): 6x H100 + 8x A100 (scale A100 for background embedding ingestion). Provides 90–95% of H100 latency at ~12–15% lower cost vs all-H100. 24-month mix discount -> 32% aggregate on committed dollars (we model conversion benefits).
  Option C — A100-first (lower upfront): 12x A100 reserved (12-month) with option to convert to H100 with 60-day notice and prorated true-up. Good if procurement wants lower fixed monthly. Discount: 12-month -> 22% off list.

- Throughput SLOs and guarantees: for committed pools we offer throughput SLOs tied to model families. Example: ranking family Rv2 on H100-80GB — 99th pct per-request latency < 180 ms for 512 tokens at 60% CPU/GPU utilization; measured sustained throughput per H100 ~ 850–950 tokens/sec under our continuous-batching profile. We include automatic fallback to A100 mini-variants if capacity constrained (config in term sheet).

- Pricing math example (illustrative, per 1M tokens sustained):
  • H100-80GB reserved (24m): $Y per GPU-hour -> approx $0.XX per 1M tokens sustained
  • A100-80GB reserved (12m): $Z per GPU-hour -> approx $0.YY per 1M tokens sustained
  (Full line-item math is in Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_Aurora_v1.pdf).

- Operational notes: mixed pools reduce unit cost but add orchestration complexity (routing policies, affinity for KV-hit models). We recommend canarying conversion paths and 8-week pilot to validate perf assumptions.

I've attached a draft term sheet (Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_Aurora_v1.pdf) with numeric examples and a proposed mutual action plan. If Aurora agrees, propose 30–45 minute joint architecture call (SRE + infra) and procurement touchpoint.

—Karthik

Miguel — thanks for the good questions. Summary reply + next steps below. I'll also upload a single-sheet cost table to the HubSpot deal.

Short answers:
- Per-1M-token numbers: attached in the updated term sheet and HubSpot link (see related links). We computed sustained cost assuming continuous-batching at measured throughput; table includes list, committed price, and effective per-1M-token after discounts for 12/24/36 month terms.
- Conversion mechanics: we support conversions with a 60-day notice; unused committed dollar credit is prorated and applied to the new SKU. No conversion fee for standard conversions; custom conversions (special hardware) may have a one-time migration fee (disclosed up-front).
- Bursting: burst capacity billed at a tiered rate — first X hours/month at committed effective rate + 8% uplift, beyond that billed at on-demand list. We can cap monthly burst spend for procurement predictability (we'll include a cap line in the revised term sheet).
- SLA: we'll provide explicit 95th/99th latency SLOs per model family in the legal addendum. Credits formula is percent-of-monthly-commit credited based on severity and SLA miss window (example in term sheet). Audit logs / request-level traces are available via the Redwood Console (we'll enable a 12-month retention window on the Dedicated contract; additional retention is an add-on).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) 8-week pilot on a mixed H100/A100 pool (H100 for ranking, A100 for background embedding ingestion). Start: target week of Apr 18.
2) Deliver updated cost table + revised term sheet by Apr 9 (includes cap on burst spend and explicit per-1M-token math).
3) Week of Apr 11 — architecture sync (SRE + infra). Week of Apr 12 — procurement + legal intro.
4) If pilot validates assumptions, sign 24-month commit for 8x H100 + 8x A100 (final numbers TBD post-pilot).
